key_insight: Humidity reshapes FAPbI₃ phase-transition pathways through competing water uptake by a layered metastable intermediate and the photo-inactive δ phase.
engineering_relevance: Understanding moisture-dependent transitions could guide humidity control during perovskite film fabrication and moisture protection during solar-cell operation.
method: Large-scale atomistic simulations using an ab initio machine-learned potential
Analysis of a layered metastable intermediate along the Burgers transition pathway
Comparison of water uptake by the intermediate and δ phase
evidence_signal: Simulations reproduce the experimentally observed rise in the δ-to-α transition temperature with increasing humidity.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative device-level validation, so implications for solar-cell performance and lifetime remain unverified.
paper_title: Humidity-modulated Ostwald Step Rule in $\rm FAPbI_3$ Martensitic Transitions
